subChunks.title: Dark Mode
subChunks.hookHtml: Dark mode is no longer a novelty feature — users expect it, and many accessibility needs depend on it. Tailwind's dark: variant lets you specify dark-mode styles inline with your light-mode classes, with no separate stylesheet required.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Two dark mode strategies in Tailwind v4

Strategy 1 — OS preference (default). No configuration needed. dark: utilities activate when the user's OS is in dark mode (prefers-color-scheme: dark).

/* index.css — nothing extra needed for OS-based dark mode */
@import "tailwindcss";

Strategy 2 — class-based toggle (recommended for production). Add one line to your CSS:

@import "tailwindcss";

/* dark: activates when html.dark is present */
@variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

Class-based lets users choose their preference independent of their OS setting. It's the correct approach for any app with a light/dark toggle.

Applying dark: styles

<div class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-900
            text-gray-900 dark:text-white
            border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700">
  Content
</div>

Unprefixed = light mode. dark: = dark mode override. Typically only needed for colour-related utilities.

Common dark mode colour mappings

bg-white           → dark:bg-gray-900
bg-gray-50         → dark:bg-gray-800
bg-gray-100        → dark:bg-gray-700
text-gray-900      → dark:text-white
text-gray-700      → dark:text-gray-200
text-gray-500      → dark:text-gray-400
border-gray-200    → dark:border-gray-700
bg-blue-100 text-blue-800 → dark:bg-blue-900/30 dark:text-blue-400

Toggling dark mode in React

function ThemeToggle() {
  const [dark, setDark] = useState(
    () => localStorage.getItem('theme') === 'dark'
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    // Must toggle on html (documentElement), not body
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark);
    localStorage.setItem('theme', dark ? 'dark' : 'light');
  }, [dark]);

  return (
    <button onClick={() => setDark(d => !d)}>
      {dark ? '☀️ Light' : '🌙 Dark'}
    </button>
  );
}

Flash of wrong theme — preventing it

<!-- In index.html, BEFORE React loads -->
<script>
  if (localStorage.theme === 'dark' ||
      (!('theme' in localStorage) &&
       window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches)) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('dark')
  }
</script>

Stacking dark with other variants

dark:hover:bg-gray-700    /* dark mode AND hovered */
dark:focus:ring-gray-500  /* dark mode AND focused */
dark:bg-blue-900/30       /* dark mode + opacity modifier */

Sable: "For a production app, always use class-based dark mode. The media strategy follows the OS and gives users no choice. The class strategy lets you put the toggle in the UI — which is what every polished app does."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: Every surface in this room has two faces — its daytime face and its night face. In Tailwind, you write both in the same place. The unprefixed class is the light face. The dark: class is what it becomes at night.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a dark-mode-ready card that looks correct in both light and dark mode:

  • .card: bg-white, dark:bg-gray-800, border, border-gray-200, dark:border-gray-700, rounded-xl, p-6, shadow-sm
  • .card-title: text-lg, font-semibold, text-gray-900, dark:text-white, mb-2
  • .card-body: text-gray-600, dark:text-gray-300, text-sm, leading-relaxed
  • .card-tag: inline-block, px-2, py-1, bg-blue-100, dark:bg-blue-900/30, text-blue-700, dark:text-blue-400, text-xs, font-medium, rounded

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a dark-mode-aware stats widget from scratch showing three stats (e.g. Users, Revenue, Uptime). The widget background, text, and border must all have both light and dark variants. Add a theme toggle button that adds/removes the dark class on the html element. No class list provided.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the two dark mode strategies in Tailwind v4 and how to configure each. What is the critical mistake when implementing the React toggle (hint: it involves which element you toggle the class on)? Why would the page flash the wrong theme on initial load, and how do you prevent it?

questions.prompt: In Tailwind v4, how do you configure class-based dark mode (activated by a dark class on <html>)?
options: It is the default — no configuration needed
questions.explanation: Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration. To activate dark mode via a class, add @variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)); to your CSS file. This tells Tailwind's dark: variant to activate when the element is inside a .dark ancestor — typically the html element. The default (without this line) is OS-preference via prefers-color-scheme: dark.

questions.prompt: You want a blue badge that uses a subtle tinted wash in dark mode — not a solid dark-blue block. Which dark mode class achieves this?
questions.explanation: The slash opacity modifier (/30) reduces the background to 30% opacity, creating a subtle tint. dark:bg-blue-900/30 is the standard pattern for coloured badges in dark mode — solid blue-900 is too heavy and looks like a block, while 30% opacity reads as a tag colour.

questions.prompt: A developer sets up class-based dark mode and adds a React toggle that calls document.body.classList.toggle('dark'). They apply dark:bg-gray-900 to the page wrapper but it never activates. What is wrong?
options: The dark class must be on document.documentElement (the html element), not document.body — Tailwind's class strategy requires the dark class on the html root
dark:bg-gray-900 is not valid — you need dark:bg-[#111] for class-based dark mode
The @variant dark rule needs to reference body instead of .dark
questions.answer: The dark class must be on document.documentElement (the html element), not document.body — Tailwind's class strategy requires the dark class on the html root
questions.explanation: This is the most common dark mode implementation mistake. Tailwind's class-based strategy generates CSS selectors that require dark to be an ancestor class on the html element (document.documentElement). The fix is document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark'). Adding it to body means it won't be a proper ancestor for all dark: selectors.
